extracted.intended_audience: NLP / machine-learning researchers working on open-domain story generation and automatic evaluation metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and training learnable automatic evaluation metrics for open-domain story generation, including constructing datasets of plausible and implausible stories and methods to produce challenging negative examples. Focus is on dataset construction (plot-guided, adversarial) and measuring correlation with human judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliable automatic evaluation metrics correlate with human judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Learnable evaluation metrics should provide more accurate assessments by having higher correlations with human judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper frames reliability of automatic metrics in terms of correlation with human judgments; this is presented as the primary success criterion for any automatic evaluator. Metrics should be validated by measuring correlation with human evaluations on generated stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learnable metrics require high-quality training data
rubrics_metrics.description: A critical bottleneck of obtaining a reliable learnable evaluation metric is the lack of high-quality training data for classifiers to efficiently distinguish plausible and implausible machine-generated stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training classifiers for evaluation requires datasets containing both plausible and implausible examples that reflect real system errors. Emphasis on dataset quality: diversity, realism, and coverage of typical failure modes influence metric reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implausible examples should be natural and not heuristically manipulated
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous works relied on 'heuristically manipulated' plausible examples to mimic system drawbacks (e.g., repetition, contradiction, irrelevant content), which can be 'unnatural' and 'oversimplify' the characteristics of implausible machine-generated stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simple, surface-level manipulations of gold/plausible text as negative examples because they may not resemble real model failures; such anti-patterns can lead to metrics that don't generalize to real generated text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use structured plots to generate targeted implausible stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate a more comprehensive set of implausible stories using plots, which are structured representations of controllable factors used to generate stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because plots are compact and structured, they are easier to manipulate to generate text with targeted undesirable properties. Dataset construction should leverage plot-level manipulations to control for specific errors while preserving naturalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain grammatical correctness and naturalness in generated implausible texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manipulations at the plot level can generate texts that maintain grammatical correctness and naturalness of the generated sentences while exhibiting undesirable properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One goal of negative-example generation is to produce implausible but fluent texts so that classifiers learn to detect subtler failures (e.g., logical inconsistency) rather than obvious noise or ungrammatical output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target specific undesirable properties (repetition, contradiction, irrelevance) when constructing negatives
rubrics_metrics.description: System drawbacks to mimic include repetition, contradiction, or irrelevant content in the text-level; these are examples of undesirable properties the dataset should cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset generation procedures should include mechanisms to induce these known failure modes so that evaluation metrics can learn to penalize them. Enumerate and ensure coverage of common error categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply adversarial filtering to select nuanced implausible texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the adversarial filtering procedure (as in Zellers et al., 2018) to select a more nuanced set of implausible texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use adversarial filtering to remove trivial negatives and keep challenging negatives that are hard for simple classifiers, improving the subtlety and usefulness of training data for learnable metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate metric improvements by measuring correlation gains vs baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics trained on the generated (plot-guided, adversarially filtered) data should result in more reliable automatic assessments that correlate better with human judgments compared to baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical validation is required: compare learned metrics trained on the proposed data to baseline metrics and report correlation with human judgments as the evaluation metric for success.
